Tables of the open data service

Source: R/odat.R
odtab.Rd

odls() lists the tables of the project's open data service and odtab() loads one by its key, as the service serves it at the time of the call. Everything about a table (its address, rows, columns and SHA-256) is read from the service's manifest at run time, so a table that its publisher has replaced is loaded as it is now, with no new release of crimlab.

Usage

odtab(
  key,
  cols = NULL,
  refresh = FALSE,
  base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev")
)

odls(base = getOption("crimlab.data", "https://data.crimlab.dev"))

Arguments

key

A table's key, as odls() lists it.

cols

The names of the columns to keep, or NULL (all).

refresh

TRUE downloads the table again even when the cache holds a copy that matches.

base

The address of the service, or of a mirror of it (a folder holding manifest.json and <db>/<table>.csv.gz, which may be a file:// address). The default is getOption("crimlab.data"), or the project's service when that is not set.

Value

odls() a data frame with a row per table: key, rows, bytes (of the gzip file), sha256 (NA for a table that cannot be checked) and columns, a list of the column names. odtab() the table as a data frame.

Details

A downloaded file is used only when its SHA-256 is the one the manifest lists. When it is not, the manifest is read once more (the table may have been replaced between the two requests) and, if the file still does not match, it is deleted and odtab() stops. A table the manifest lists without a SHA-256 cannot be checked and is not loaded.

Tables are kept in tools::R_user_dir("crimlab", "cache"). A kept file is used again only while its SHA-256 is the one the manifest lists now; otherwise, or with refresh = TRUE, the table is downloaded again.

The columns are those of the file, named as served. cols picks some of them, matched without regard to case or underscores ("case_id" finds "CaseID"), so that a publisher's respelling of a name does not break a call; an exact name is preferred.

Errors: a key the manifest does not list; a table listed without a SHA-256; a file that does not match it; a column the table does not have, or a name that matches more than one; a service that cannot be reached, answers with an error or does not answer in time (60 seconds for the manifest, 600 for a table, or getOption("timeout") if longer).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# needs the internet
tabs <- odls()
head(tabs[, c("key", "rows")])
x <- odtab(tabs$key[!is.na(tabs$sha256)][1L])
str(x)
} # }
